issues.description: Stale comments still reference Python 3.9/3.10 compatibility after the gate is removed
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py keeps the comment 'this is for < 3.10 compatibility' above default_raise, and the function itself is preserved with that justification. With 3.9 gone the rationale no longer holds; either delete default_raise or rewrite the comment to state the real invariant (kw_only dataclasses with no default forbid positional construction). Readers will be misled.

issues.description: pairwise replacement is correct but the loop invariant should be stated
issues.detail: The change from zip(ordered, ordered[1:]) to itertools.pairwise(ordered) is semantically equivalent and avoids an O(n) slice allocation. Worth a one-line comment stating the invariant: 'for every adjacent pair (a, b) in sorted order, a.before(b) holds.' Otherwise a future reader must re-derive why pairwise suffices.

issues.description: Dead 'pragma: no cover' branches and obsolete comments left behind
issues.detail: conditions.py keeps a 'continue' whose long explanatory comment about 3.9 coverage quirks was deleted, but similar pragma/comment vestiges (e.g. default_raise's 'pragma: no cover', the wallet_request_types comment block above TransactionEndpointRequest mentioning '< 3.10 compatibility') should be swept in the same pass. Literate code should not carry archaeological notes about a version it no longer supports.

issues.description: install.sh version-range check is now inconsistent with the stated minimum
issues.detail: The guard reads PYTHON_MINOR_VER -lt 7, but the user-facing message says '>= 3.10 and < 3.13'. The numeric check still admits 3.7-3.9 silently before the message fires. Tighten to -lt 10 so the invariant 'accepted iff message-stated range' actually holds; right now the implementation and the documentation disagree.

issues.description: find_python ordering preserved but worth a comment on the invariant
issues.detail: The loop 'for V in 312 3.12 311 3.11 310 3.10 3' encodes 'prefer newest, fall back to bare python3 last.' Now that 39/3.9 are gone the intent is clearer, but the invariant ('BEST_VERSION holds the highest available supported minor, or empty') is still implicit. One literate comment would let a reader audit correctness without tracing the shell.

review.summary: A clean, mechanical removal of 3.9 support: CI matrices, install scripts, dataclass kw_only gates, and poetry markers all move in lockstep, and the algorithmic substitution of itertools.pairwise for zip(seq, seq[1:]) is asymptotically and semantically correct. The lens flags residual literate-programming debt rather than algorithmic faults: several comments still cite 'for < 3.10 compatibility' next to code that now unconditionally requires 3.10, and one helper (default_raise) survives with a rationale that no longer applies. install.sh's numeric guard (-lt 7) lags the user-visible '>= 3.10' message, so the check and the documentation no longer agree. No complexity regressions, no data-structure mistakes, no premature optimization — just a sweep needed for the prose layer.
